free_tier.stated: A free virtual machine on real IBM LinuxONE hardware on the s390x architecture, with full root via sudo, described by IBM as "a free, enterprise-grade, 24/7 cloud platform" where you "can get up to 120 days of free access - just register for a virtual machine and you're in" and "no cost, no credit card". The registration form's own heading reads "Sign up to get a 120-day complimentary trial".
free_tier.notes: the unit is a whole machine for a fixed term, not an allowance in hours; IBM publishes no shape, no egress term and no hourly figure

per_object_cap.notes: the ceiling that matters is the machine shape, which IBM does not publish; third-party reports put it at 2 vCPU, 4 GB and 40-50 GB of disk

retention.stated: The server is granted for up to 120 days in two steps, 60 days and then a further 60 days, and the user must extend it at the 60-day mark after a reminder email.
retention.notes: a machine record: what is lost is the running process and the disk, not a stored object; the account page carries an 'Expiration Date' field, and there is a service/extend endpoint behind an emailed token

egress.terms: not published on any page read: no egress term, traffic allowance or bandwidth figure appears in the terms, the registration form or the deployment guide, so nothing is asserted

interface_detail: SSH with a key pair only: the terms state 'Only SSH keys are allowed.', and the deployment guide states that an SSH public key is required to deploy an instance and that sudo gives root authority
tooling: any SSH client with a key pair; ports other than SSH are opened with iptables on the instance
chaining: The only free compute on this list with a non-x86 architecture, so it is the cheap way to build and test s390x artifacts without QEMU emulation, and it pairs with an x86 free tier that does the packaging.

limits.value: 120 days, then all resources are cleared of data and returned to the pool
registration is not automatic: 'Your registration is under review. Your request may take up to one (1) business day to process.'
one virtual server per account: the create-instance page refuses a second with 'There is an instance existing, delete the old one and then deploy this new one.'

binding_note: The 120-day term binds: the machine is wiped and returned to the pool at expiry, so it cannot be an always-on box beyond four months without a new registration.

identity_cost.detail: The live registration form asks for an email address, a password, a first and last name, a country, a project description of 75 to 500 characters, and a Terms checkbox; the Organization field carries no required attribute; no card, no phone and no identity document. The phone and SMS-code block is present in the page source but commented out, and the controller that submits the form posts no phone field at all. One account per email address, and outlook.com and hotmail.com addresses are refused by the registration system.

reliability_note: The portal's status line has shown 'Cloud Status: Stopped' and users reported the virtual-machine service as unavailable in July 2026; there are no backups, so an expiry or an outage takes the disk.

notes: SIGNUP PATH, read. The account is created at https://linuxone.cloud.marist.edu/#/register?flag=VM, reached from IBM's front door at community.ibm.com/zsystems/l1cc/ by the 'Try Virtual Machines' link. The form is an Angular template, and its source lists: email, password and confirmation, first name, last name, organization, country (a 242-option list defaulting to United States, with Viet Nam present), a project description of 75 to 500 characters, an optional event code, a Terms checkbox and reCAPTCHA v3. THE PHONE STEP IS GONE. The form in circulation, including IBM's own archived deployment guide, says 'Provide a mobile phone number that is capable of receiving SMS messages', and the live page still carries that block in its source - but it is inside HTML comments, the controller's submit payload has no phone field, and the SMS-code function is commented out. So the phone claim is superseded, and the row is email-only, which is why identity_cost.kind is 'email' rather than 'any-phone'. NO CARD, NO ADDRESS. address1 through zip are posted as empty strings by the controller. Organization is on the form but has no required attribute. WHAT STOPS A SIGNUP: manual review, not a gate. The form's own success message says the request 'may take up to one (1) business day to process' and that credentials arrive by email once approved, and it also has a refusal path, 'We need additional information to proceed with your registration.' IBM's front door additionally states that outlook.com and hotmail.com addresses are currently refused by the registration system, which is a documented, first-party, signup-level failure and the cheapest one to avoid. WHAT IT GRANTS: one virtual server, s390x, full sudo, a public IP, SSH-key-only access, 120 days. THE SHAPE IS STILL UNPUBLISHED. IBM names the flavors LinuxONE-Small and LinuxONE-Medium and never states their vCPU, memory or disk; the 2 vCPU / 4 GB / 40 GB figure is third-party and is marked as such. The console fetches flavor values at runtime, so they are not readable without an account. NETWORK: the instance gets a public IP and a firewall that opens only SSH, so inbound listening works but every port has to be opened with iptables first; that is documented in IBM's deployment guide. EGRESS IS UNPUBLISHED; the vendor can instead throttle or terminate for 'excessive network, computing or other resources'. VERDICT CHANGED to trial-only from qualifies-with-caveat. The grant is a fixed 120-day term after which 'all resources will be cleared of your data', which is a trial with a hard stop and not a renewable free tier; the earlier verdict was written when the 120-day term was read as a re-registration cycle, and no page says a re-registration succeeds. An extension mechanism exists in the portal (a service/extend endpoint behind an emailed token) but nothing states that a virtual-server entitlement is eligible for it.
